---
title: "Class-structured populations"
subtitle: "Otto & Day, chapter 10, with PracticalCAS"
engine: julia
---

When individuals differ by age, stage or location, the population is a vector
and one time step is multiplication by a projection matrix. Its dominant
eigenvalue is the long-term growth factor, the right eigenvector the stable
class distribution, the left eigenvector the reproductive values.

```{julia}
using PracticalCAS
@syms λ s₁::(0, 1) s₂::(0, 1) f₁::positive f₂::positive f₃::positive
```

## A Leslie matrix

Three age classes: fecundities `fᵢ` and survival `sᵢ` from class `i` to `i+1`.

```{julia}
L = leslie([f₁, f₂, f₃], [s₁, s₂])
```

Its characteristic equation is the Euler–Lotka equation: with survivorship
`l₁ = 1`, `l₂ = s₁`, `l₃ = s₁ s₂`, the growth factor solves
`Σ λ⁻ˣ lₓ fₓ = 1`.

```{julia}
el = euler_lotka([1, s₁, s₁ * s₂], [f₁, f₂, f₃], λ)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
cp = charpoly(L, λ)
@assert isequiv(cp, -λ^3 * (el.lhs - el.rhs)) || isequiv(cp, λ^3 * (el.lhs - el.rhs))
```

## A numerical example

```{julia}
Ln = leslie([0, 1, 4], [1 // 2, 1 // 4])
vals = eigvals(Ln)
```

```{julia}
λ₁ = only(filter(v -> isreal(v) && evalf(v) > 0, vals))
```

The stable age distribution and the reproductive values:

```{julia}
w = stable_distribution(Ln, λ₁)
```

```{julia}
v = reproductive_values(Ln, λ₁)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert λ₁ == 1
@assert all(isequiv.(Ln * w, w)) && isequiv(sum(w), 1)

@assert all(isequiv.(permutedims(v) * Ln, permutedims(v)))
@assert isequiv(w[1], 8 // 13)
```

The elasticities of `λ` to each entry sum to one: here the population is most
sensitive to survival to the second age class.

```{julia}
ela = elasticity(Ln, λ₁)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(sum(ela), 1)
@assert isequiv(ela[2, 1], 2 // 5) && evalf(ela[2, 1]) == maximum(evalf.(ela))
S = sensitivity(Ln, λ₁)
# check one sensitivity by differentiating λ along the entry
@syms h
Lh = symbolic(Ln); Lh[2, 1] = Lh[2, 1] + h
cph = charpoly(Lh, λ)
dλ = -subs(diff(cph, h), h => 0, λ => 1) / subs(diff(cph, λ), h => 0, λ => 1)
@assert isequiv(S[2, 1], dλ)
```

## The general solution

`n(t) = Lᵗ n(0)`; in the long run every class grows by the factor `λ₁` and the
distribution approaches `w`:

```{julia}
@syms t::natural
Lt = matpow(Ln, t)
nt = Lt * [10, 0, 0]
[evalf(subs(x, t => 40)) for x in nt] ./ evalf(subs(sum(nt), t => 40))
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
fr = [evalf(subs(x, t => 40)) for x in nt] ./ evalf(subs(sum(nt), t => 40))
@assert all(abs.(fr .- evalf.(w)) .< 1e-3)
@assert all(isapprox.(evalf.(subs(Lt, t => 3)), evalf(Ln^3); atol = 1e-10))
```

## Continuous time: a stage-structured model

Juveniles mature at rate `m` and die at rate `μⱼ`; adults reproduce at rate
`b` and die at rate `μₐ`. The population grows when the dominant eigenvalue
of the rate matrix is positive, which happens exactly when an individual
replaces itself, `R₀ = b m / ((m + μⱼ) μₐ) > 1`:

```{julia}
@syms J::nonneg A::nonneg m::positive μⱼ::positive μₐ::positive b::positive
st = ode(J => b * A - (m + μⱼ) * J, A => m * J - μₐ * A)
R₀ = reproduction_number([b * A, 0], [(m + μⱼ) * J, μₐ * A - m * J], [J, A], Dict(J => 0, A => 0))
```

```{julia}
stability(st, Dict(J => 0, A => 0)).condition
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(R₀, b * m / ((m + μⱼ) * μₐ))
c0 = stability(st, Dict(J => 0, A => 0)).condition
@assert decide(subs(c0, b => 1, m => 1, μⱼ => 1, μₐ => 1)) === true     # R₀ = 1/2
@assert decide(subs(c0, b => 4, m => 1, μⱼ => 1, μₐ => 1)) === false    # R₀ = 2

```
